5 microhabits to make you the
most confident person in any room

saying names

use people's names once when you talk to them, especially people you've just met. it's a tiny habit, but it makes you sound sure of yourself and makes them feel noticed.

the first hello

be the first to say hello in every room you walk into this week, even in a lift or a waiting room. starting the moment yourself is a small act that makes everything after it easier.

one thing to share

spend 5 minutes a day learning one surprising story from history or science. having something interesting to share means you never walk into a room worried about what to say.
slides.texte_sophia:
one thing to share

i spend 5 minutes a day learning one surprising story from history or science. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and i never worry about what to say anymore.

slides.texte_overlay:
asking for directions

ask a stranger for directions or a recommendation once a day, even when you don't need it. tiny, low-stakes conversations are how talking to anyone stops feeling scary.

ordering out loud

order at the counter instead of on your phone, and ask one question about the menu. speaking up in small everyday moments trains the same muscle you need in the big ones.
